title: Signal · Friday 20 November
overview: UBS and the Swiss Bankers Association reject key parts of the banking stability package, the ECB finds gaps in cyber and ICT controls at 92 percent of the banks it supervises, and JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard say vendor breaches exposed customer data.

top.headline: UBS and the Swiss Bankers Association reject key parts of the banking stability package
top.summary: In consultation responses published on 19 November, UBS said it rejects significant portions of the Federal Council's third too-big-to-fail package, and the Swiss Bankers Association called it excessive and unbalanced. Both oppose wider FINMA powers and the senior managers regime as proposed; UBS also rejects mandatory rotation of the regulatory audit firm and early intervention without objective triggers.
top.background: The Federal Council opened the consultations on 12 August: about 30 measures drawn from the Credit Suisse collapse, covering liquidity, resolution and supervision. The SBA backs faster access to central bank liquidity in a crisis.
top.why: The package decides how far FINMA can reach into the management of every Swiss bank; UBS estimates about 150 of its people would need individual FINMA approval, according to AWP.
top.watch_next: A National Council committee debates the separate UBS capital bill in detail on 23 and 24 November.

top.headline: ECB finds gaps in cyber, third-party and ICT controls at 92 percent of banks
top.summary: Publishing its 2026 supervisory review of 108 banks on 19 November, the ECB kept overall CET1 requirements and guidance broadly stable at 11.3 percent of risk-weighted assets for 2027, against 11.2 percent for 2026. Operational and ICT risk remained among the weakest-scoring areas: 92 percent of significant institutions showed deficiencies in cybersecurity, third-party risk management and ICT risk controls.
top.background: Its priorities for 2027 to 2029 include on-site cyber and third-party inspections, threat-led penetration testing under DORA and reviews of cloud dependencies. Supervisors will also assess banks' responses to AI-enabled cyber threats and their readiness for post-quantum cryptography.
top.why: For euro area banks, supervisory pressure is shifting from capital to ICT remediation, cloud concentration and AI-driven threats, where most score changes now originate.

top.headline: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard say vendors' breaches exposed some customer data
top.summary: JPMorganChase said on 19 November that third parties providing services to it were the target of a cyberattack, and that attackers accessed marketing data that may include customer names and email addresses. Mastercard reported exposed email addresses for a subset of cardholders in one benefit programme, and Visa traced its incident to a provider in Asia Pacific. All three said payments were unaffected.
top.background: A ransomware group called n0n claimed the attack, according to the Wall Street Journal as cited by Quartz; Cybernews counted about 16,000 JPMorgan customers in the leaked files.
top.why: The data taken was low-grade, but it left through marketing and loyalty vendors, the kind of outer supplier that third-party risk inventories can miss.
top.watch_next: Whether the vendors are named and other banks report incidents through the same platforms.

items.headline: EBA says EU banks already make extensive use of frontier AI models
items.summary: In its Autumn 2026 Risk Assessment Report, published on 19 November, the EBA said banks expect AI to improve productivity and already use frontier models to detect system weaknesses and strengthen controls. It warned that AI may raise exposure to cyberattacks and fraud, and adds model risk and dependence on external providers.
items.why: Gives EU supervisors a documented basis to question how banks govern frontier models and which outside providers they depend on.

items.headline: SIX starts using Rivero's Amiko for debit card fraud and dispute claims
items.summary: SIX has launched Amiko, the fraud recovery and dispute platform of Swiss fintech Rivero, for its debit card business, starting with one partner bank and expanding in phases. Cardholders report fraud or dispute a payment in the debiX+ app, guided by a virtual agent, and a complete claim is created at first contact.
items.why: SIX issues and processes debit cards for more than 100 banks in Switzerland and Liechtenstein, so the change reaches customers of many smaller banks.

items.headline: Twint adds a hybrid merchant fee and a tool comparing payment costs
items.summary: Merchants with a direct Twint contract can keep the Basis model at 1.3 percent per transaction or choose a new Hybrid model: a flat 9 rappen below CHF 10, and 0.99 percent plus 9 rappen from CHF 10, according to finews. Twint also launched a tool comparing providers' entry terms.
items.why: Puts a published price comparison from Switzerland's bank-owned payment app in front of merchants while the Federal Council consults on fee transparency.

items.headline: Tether invests in Swiss platform Scrypt to expand stablecoin payments for institutions
items.summary: Scrypt, a Swiss platform for round-the-clock trading, payments and custody of crypto assets, announced a strategic investment by Tether, issuer of the largest dollar stablecoin, according to finews. The funds are to support its expansion into third-party payments, so banks, brokers and payment firms can settle cross-border transactions in stablecoins.
items.why: Gives Swiss banks a local route to stablecoin settlement without building it, as the Swiss Bankers Association pushes for bank-issued franc stablecoins.

items.headline: UBS to move hundreds of group function roles from Europe to India, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: UBS plans to shift hundreds of roles in finance, operations, risk control, compliance, legal and human resources to India over the next couple of years, according to Bloomberg, as reported by swissinfo. Most are junior to mid-level roles now held in Poland, outside the 3,000 Swiss job cuts tied to the integration. UBS declined to comment.
items.why: Shows the integration's cost drive reaching control functions; the report says India also gives UBS more capacity to build AI into its systems.

items.headline: Update: UBS property funds buy the Üetlihof for CHF 850 million
items.summary: Norges Bank Investment Management signed an agreement on 19 November to sell the Üetlihof office complex in Zurich to four Swiss real estate funds of UBS Asset Management for CHF 850 million, according to finews. Closing is planned for January 2027, and UBS stays on as long-term tenant.
items.why: Leaves UBS funds owning a site whose tenant is the UBS Group, an arrangement fund investors may watch closely.

items.headline: PostFinance lifts nine-month operating profit by CHF 58 million to CHF 282 million
items.summary: PostFinance raised its operating result for the first nine months of 2026 by CHF 58 million to CHF 282 million, driven by fee and payment income and lower costs, according to AWP via investrends. Interest income remained under pressure from zero rates. Customer assets rose CHF 3.1 billion since the end of 2025 to CHF 116.9 billion.
items.why: Confirms that payments and cost control, rather than interest income, carry Switzerland's postal bank while rates stay at zero.

items.headline: ING aims to double wealth revenues within five years as it expands private banking
items.summary: ING wants its wealth business to double revenues in five years, about 15 percent growth a year, Anneka Treon, its global head of private banking, wealth management and investments, told WealthBriefing. The bank opened private banking in Spain and Italy in early November for clients with EUR 500,000 or more and uses digital tools to move savers into investments.
items.why: Adds a digital-first rival for affluent clients in the European markets where Swiss private banks run onshore operations.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic shares close 17 percent above the IPO price on their first day
items.summary: Anthropic's shares traded at USD 111.50 in their first minutes on Nasdaq on 19 November, 33 percent above the USD 83 offer price, according to TechCrunch. They closed up 17.07 percent at USD 97.17 after touching USD 115, according to AFP via Allnews. The offering raised a record USD 81.3 billion.
items.why: Makes the maker of Claude a listed company with quarterly reporting, giving enterprise buyers more visibility on its finances and priorities.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent showed staff other users' messages and bank balances, Reuters reports
items.summary: Meta employees raised concerns in internal posts that the Muse agent mixed up conversations across accounts, surfacing childcare requests, product orders and bank account balances that were not theirs, according to a Reuters report cited by TechCrunch. Meta said employees test versions of Muse that differ from the public app, which has more than 10 million downloads.
items.why: Shows the account-mixing risk banks face when customers let agents read their apps, the issue behind Citi's and PNC's new liability terms.

items.headline: Databricks restarts clusters to shield customers from the Java4Shell OpenJDK flaw
items.summary: Databricks said on 19 November it had applied a mitigation that disables the vulnerable code in all supported Databricks Runtime versions, taking the rare step of proactively restarting affected clusters, and will release patched runtimes. It called Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) an industry-wide OpenJDK vulnerability and said it had no evidence of unauthorised access.
items.why: Java runs much of the banking and data stack, so bank IT teams and their vendors face the same choice between quick mitigation and disruptive restarts.

items.headline: EU Commission confirms cyberattack in which attackers reportedly used the AI tool Artex
items.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted internal platforms, including the Sysper HR system, for more than ten days, according to Politico as reported by Inside IT. CERT-EU detected the campaign in early November, and the attackers are said to have used Artex, a publicly available AI-supported tool, to find weaknesses.
items.why: A week after the FBI warned that Artex was being used against financial firms, it shows automated attack tools reaching the EU's own executive.

items.headline: Google lets the Gemini app operate Mac apps, files and websites for users
items.summary: Google added computer use to the Gemini app for Mac on 19 November. Users describe a workflow and Gemini clicks, types and fills in forms across local files, desktop apps and the web in a separate window, while users choose which apps it may access and approve actions before they run.
items.why: Desktop agents from the major labs now compete for the same Mac workflows, so firms need rules on which agent may touch which apps and data.

say_it_today: The ECB found gaps in cyber, third-party and ICT controls at 92 percent of the banks it supervises directly, in the same week JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard traced customer data losses to their vendors. For banks, the exposure increasingly sits with suppliers.
